//: W7-C3 (bd forge-opj): the tsc project that typechecks forge-ui's TEST
files. Before this, NO tsc project saw them — forge-ui/tsconfig.json
excludes **/*.test.ts (so `next build` stays off them) and the root
tsconfig has no forge-ui at all; vitest transpiles WITHOUT typechecking,
so a type-level assertion in a test (e.g. a union-exhaustiveness pin, or
studio-client.test.ts's Run['origin'] admission pin) could never fail
any gate. This project is its own CI step (`UI tests typecheck`),
SEPARATE from the build gate: under test-first development a pinned-red
test may legitimately import a not-yet-created module mid-branch — the
gate binds at PR time, when the suite is green.
NOTE the base tsconfig's own exclude comment says test files 'run via
node --test' — that is true for orchestrator/cli tests but forge-ui/lib
tests run under VITEST (vitest.config.ts include: lib/components); the
real reason for the exclusion there is keeping tsc/next off the tests,
which this sibling project now covers.
next-env.d.ts and .next/ are EXCLUDED (the base project keeps both).
Several parity pins deliberately cross-import an orchestrator SSOT module
(work-item.ts, flow-trigger.ts, config.ts, studio/validate-triggers.ts) so
the client copy of a vocabulary is checked against the real one. Those
modules are owned and typechecked by the ROOT tsconfig; pulling Next's
global augmentations in here would rejudge them under forge-ui's lib —
Next declares ProcessEnv.NODE_ENV REQUIRED, which the root project does
not — and report errors on orchestrator code from a forge-ui gate. Worse,
it made the result depend on whether .next/ happened to be built. next/*
types the tests actually use (next/link, next/navigation) resolve from
node_modules either way.
